html:
Three things outlive a run: the project file, a link that carries the project to someone else, and the recording of the last two minutes of the machine. This chapter is about all three, and about using the recording to debug. Being able to wind a machine back and watch the scan where it went wrong is something no real line gives you.

The project file

File → Save (Ctrl+S) writes one .json file holding everything: the scene and every device’s settings, the tags, the routines, the I/O configuration and, if you tick it, the network settings. File → Open reads it back. The page also keeps your work by itself between visits, so the file is for versions and for moving a project to another PC.

A share link

File → Share Link… packs the same project into the address itself. The JSON is deflated and written after #lc=, so nothing is uploaded anywhere: whoever has the link has the project.

Opening a link asks first, with a summary of what is in it, because it replaces the project you have open. The project you have open is put aside first (a level keeps its program, the sandbox project comes back as My sandbox project), and your other levels are kept. In the desktop app, File → Open Link… takes a pasted link, or the whole message it came in.

Watch For

Some mail and chat apps cut very long links short. A link cut short is refused with a clear message rather than opening half a project. For a big scene (over about 60 KB of link, which the dialog warns about) send the file instead.

The scene recorder

While a sandbox scene runs, the recorder keeps a frame every 0.25 s of machine time for the last two minutes (one minute on a phone). A frame holds every part on the floor, every device’s state (a timer half run, a cylinder half out, a tank’s level and temperature, a case on the packer’s lane), the simulator’s counters and log, the machine faults you injected, the random generator that picks the part mix, and every tag in the controller.

The bar under the simulator toolbar shows the span recorded, REC 0:00.05 – 0:40.38. Drag the slider back, or press ◀, and the scene goes into REPLAY:

Because the random generator is rewound with everything else, running on from a frame with the same program gives the same run, bottle for bottle. Change a rung and run on from the same frame, and the only difference between the two runs is your change. That is the most useful thing the recorder does.

Try it: catch a jam and read the scan

Run the bottle line. After a few bottles, use Tools → Inject Machine Fault… → Jam. The jammed bottle stops, LS11 does not see it where the registers say it should be, Alarm_Word bit 2 sets and the line stops. Switch to Program mode, open S11_Alarms and drag the slider back a second at a time to the frame where EOL_Missing first goes true. The rung above it shows why: LS11 dark while the Exist and Large bits said a bottle was due. Now drag back to before you injected the jam and press Run from here. The jam is gone, because the fault was injected after that moment and the recorder rewinds faults with the rest. The line runs as if it had never happened.

Try it: prove a change on the same run

On Level 10, run until the first case creeps onto the mark under the packer head, then scrub back to the frame where Case_Slow makes. Note where the case stops: on the mark. Change the creep rung from MOV(15,Case_Hz) to MOV(30,Case_Hz), accept the edit and press Run from here. The same case, on the same frame, now runs past the head before Case_In_Place can stop it, because at 30 Hz the drive’s 0.5 s decel ramp carries it beyond the ±6 px window. With no case under the head nothing is packed, and the case goes out empty for −25. Put 15 back, scrub to the same frame, run from here again, and it lands. Two runs that differ only in one number.

What is and is not rewound

Rewound: the parts, the devices, the controller’s tags (timers, counters, ONS bits, arrays, UDTs), its periodic task schedule, the machine faults and the random part mix. Not rewound: your program and the scene layout (they are what you are testing), the trend charts, and anything outside the page: a real device on the bridge, or an EtherNet/IP module. Reset Sim, New Order or opening another project starts a new recording.
